unitKey: 2Solid, liquid, gas states and changes of stateChemistry

questions.question: What can be said about the condensing point and boiling point of water?
options: They are different temperatures; condensing is 0°C and boiling is 100°C.
They are the same temperature, which is 100°C.
Water does not have a condensing point, only a boiling point.
The boiling point is 100°C, but the condensing point is 50°C.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes what steam is?
options: Water in the solid state.
Water in the liquid state.
Water in the gas state.
A mixture of air and liquid water droplets.

questions.question: When a liquid is boiled to become a gas, what happens to the overall volume of the substance?
options: It increases.
It decreases.
It stays exactly the same.
It fluctuates randomly.

questions.question: How do the positions of particles change during the processes of boiling and condensing?
options: Particles move closer together when boiled and further apart when condensed.
Particles move further apart when boiled and move closer together when condensed.
Particles stay at the same distance but vibrate faster when boiled.
Particles clump together during boiling and spread out during condensing.

questions.question: What happens to a Bunsen burner flame when you open the air hole?
options: It becomes yellow, cooler, and silent.
It changes from orange and sooty to a hotter, cleaner, blue flame.
It goes out immediately.
It changes from a blue flame to a cooler, orange, sooty flame.

questions.question: What is the safe way to carry a lit splint in a science laboratory?
options: Hold it completely upright above your head.
Run quickly with the flame pointed forward to keep it lit.
Hold it with the flame angled slightly downwards and shield it with your other hand.
Keep it in a horizontal position with both hands on the wooden end.

questions.question: When comparing states of matter, which state has the least energy and which has the most energy?
options: Liquid has the least, gas has the most.
Solid has the least, liquid has the most.
Solid has the least, gas has the most.
Gas has the least, solid has the most.

questions.question: At what temperatures can a substance in its liquid state evaporate?
options: Only at its exact boiling point.
Only at temperatures above its boiling point.
At temperatures below its boiling point.
Only when it is heated to 100°C or higher.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the evaporation of water is correct?
options: Water can only evaporate when it reaches 100°C.
Water evaporates at temperatures that are lower than 100°C.
Water never evaporates below 50°C.
Water cannot evaporate at room temperature.

questions.question: What state change occurs when a substance undergoes freezing?
options: It changes from the liquid state to the solid state.
It changes from the solid state to the liquid state.
It changes from the gas state to the liquid state.
It changes from the liquid state to the gas state.

questions.question: For a pure substance, how do its melting point and freezing point compare?
options: The melting point is always higher than the freezing point.
The freezing point is always higher than the melting point.
They are the same temperature.
They depend entirely on the pressure and are never equal.

questions.question: How does the strength of the forces of attraction between particles affect a substance's melting point?
options: Stronger forces of attraction mean a lower melting point.
Stronger forces of attraction mean a higher melting point.
The strength of forces of attraction has no effect on the melting point.
Stronger forces of attraction mean the substance cannot be melted.

questions.question: What are the approximate temperatures for the freezing point of water, typical room temperature, and normal human body temperature?
options: Water freezes at 0°C, room temp is about 20°C, and body temp is about 37°C.
Water freezes at 10°C, room temp is about 25°C, and body temp is about 98°C.
Water freezes at 0°C, room temp is about 37°C, and body temp is about 20°C.
Water freezes at -5°C, room temp is about 20°C, and body temp is about 37°C.

questions.question: How do the particles of a substance behave when it is in the gas state?
options: They are tightly packed and vibrate in fixed positions.
They are close together but can slide past one another slowly.
They are moving very quickly in random directions with gaps between them.
They remain completely still and are evenly spaced out.

questions.question: What exists in the spaces between the particles of a gas?
options: Air.
Nothing at all.
Tiny dust particles.
Water vapor.

questions.question: Which properties describe a substance in its liquid state?
options: It has a fixed shape, cannot flow, and can be compressed.
It can flow, fills the shape of its container, and cannot be compressed.
It can flow, fills the whole of a container, and can be compressed.
It has a fixed shape, can flow, and cannot be compressed.
